..
Look for shower potential to increase during the next 12 to 24 hours,
as a subtle surface trough passes overhead. Originally, the models
portrayed this as the leading edge of stronger 15 to 20 knot trade
winds, but, this morning's scatterometer pass showed these winds have
already expanded west-southwest across the region ahead of the
trough. This is due to the pressure gradient tightening a little
faster than the models show, which was anticipated, as high pressure
continues to strengthen to the north between Iwo To and 
Minamitorishima. It wouldn't be surprising if we end up seeing 
sustained winds increase from 15 to 20 knots currently analyzed in 
the surge, into the 20 to 25 knot range by week's end. 

Although the trough is passing overhead tonight, moisture is 
somewhat anemic for this time of year. As such, look for mainly 
isolated showers to develop tonight. Additional troughs upstream 
towards Wake Island will lead to periods of scattered showers 
developing as we head towards the weekend. Depending on trough 
amplitude, if enough moisture flux and surface convergence develop, 
isolated thunderstorms couldn't be ruled out, although omega values 
are rather paltry in the time height soundings. Still, it's something
we'll keep an eye on.

Marine...
Moderate to fresh winds will prevail through the weekend. Isolated
gusts near 25 knots can't be ruled out the next 24 hours, mainly near
any stronger shower that develops. However, temporal and areal
coverage looks insufficient to hoist an advisory at this time. Seas
of 4 to 6 feet will build a foot towards the weekend, when scattered
showers could develop as well.

Fire weather...
The KBDI continues to climb, with todays reading up to 528, which is
in the high category. Sustained winds of 15 to 20 mph will persist 
during the late morning through late afternoon hours from Guam north 
to Saipan this week. Wind gusts to 30 mph are possible, especially 
for higher elevations. However, todays numerical runs indicate 
humidity values will remain above 60%. Thus, it remains to be seen if
a Fire Weather Watch will be needed. Given the persistent dry 
conditions, with a good amount of dry fuel moisture available, wild 
fire starts are possible. Folks are urged to monitor any outdoor-
related activities that involve a spark or flames this week, as 
elevated conditions are present.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) has now become more active, with
bands of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms found over
Pohnpei and Majuro, but well north of Kosrae. Over the next several
days, the NET looks to meander around the region, bringing periods of
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for Majuro through
Wednesday night, at Pohnpei tonight and near the end of the week and
finally, at Kosrae near the end of the week into the weekend. 
Rainfall amounts still look to remain relatively low, so it is still 
highly recommended to conserve water and use catchments to gather as
much of the rainwater as possible over the next few days. This dry 
season still promises to well below normal rainfall across the 
region.

No major changes made to the marine forecast. increasing trade swell
is still expected later in the week and over the weekend, with seas
reaching up to seven feet in Pohnpei and Kosrae and up to 8 Feet for
Majuro. Light to gentle trade winds are still expected to become
gentle to moderate, with occasional strong gusts possible, later in
the week into the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
The NET that was hovering in the southern portion of western 
Micronesia has moved further north than previously expected. This has
brought scattered to numerous showers along the axis, with scattered
showers near Palau and numerous near Chuuk, Yap will likely dodge 
the northern extent of the NET. While these showers will bring some 
much needed rain to many islands it is not anticipated to be enough 
to slight the drought category up a notch. With that being said, 
this would be a perfect opportunity to catch rain and top off water 
reserves. 

The north swell continues slowly subsiding. Combined seas of 5 to 7
feet are seen across the region. The north swell has shifted to 
northeast a bit early. Seas are forecast to maintain the 5 to 7 foot
range through the week. This will keep surf around 7 to 8 feet. Seas
and surf are expected to remain below advisory thresholds of 10 foot
seas and 9 foot surf. Light to moderate winds are expected to build 
to gentle to fresh for the middle of the week before tapering down to
light to moderate for the weekend.
